**Spending the margin (two cuts):**
- **Third 16 px epoch, priority 5.** Port the 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 schedule onto E044. This was a near-miss in E029/E040. Expected about 5.00 s (around -4.5%) at 0.7525-0.755, so it is roughly a coin flip on feasibility.

**Making sure the margin is real:**
- **Margin check, priority 3 (H4.2.3, rebased onto E044).** An identical rerun of E044 plus a side run on seeds 3-10. E044's +0.32 pp gain comes from a single run, and the noise on a difference between two runs is about 0.2 pp.

**Zero-cost accuracy knobs:**
- **Head Muon learning rate at 0.5x, priority 3 (H7).** The head's update size was copied from the conv filters without tuning, and E044 just showed the head is a real accuracy lever.
- **Halved warmup, priority 2 (H6.4.1, rebased onto E044).**

**Cuts that should carry over to the official 300 W PCIe GPU:**
- **Group 2 width 352, priority 3 (H2.13.1).** It reduces compute, so it should hold up on the slower judging GPU. With Muon's flatter epoch slope it may now trade at 0.06 pp or less per 1% of time.
- **Faster prepare, priority 2 (H2.4).** Prepare's ~60 ms is ~1% of the run and is no longer hidden behind power-capped training.

**Measurement:**
- **Per-phase profiling, priority 2 (H2.4.2).** It splits each phase into augmentation, forward/backward, optimizer and idle gaps. The result decides whether CUDA graphs (H2.12.1) or pre-downsampling the data for the low-res phases are worth running.

**Dropped:** I053. Its base (E035 at bs 1024) is out of date, its best case saves under 1.6%, and the profiling run measures the same small-map cost floor anyway.

**Deliberately left out:**
- **Muon LR floor (H6.5.1):** a low prior, since lowering the LR floor didn't help under SGD (E015).
- **Muon tuning:** already closed (momentum, LR, Newton-Schulz count and label smoothing all gave nothing usable).
- **Batch-size changes:** exhausted (E043)."}

ideas.description: On the E044 tip (bs 1536, compiled batched Muon on the 9 group convs plus the 576->100 head, renorm every 2+int(15*progress) steps, 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs), change only the schedule to 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, so epoch 2 moves from 24 px to 16 px. This is the E029/E040 near-miss moved onto the base that has margin. Keep the operator the same: flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear downsample, with AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1). The step count is unchanged, so LR, EMA, lookahead and renorm are unchanged. The 1536-batch 16 px shape is already warmed up in build. New tip only under the H4 rule.
ideas.expected: Time about 4.98-5.03 s (-4 to -5% vs 5.237 s): one 24 px epoch (~0.50 s at bs 1536) becomes a 16 px epoch (~0.27 s). Accuracy 0.7525-0.7550: E044's 0.7574 minus the 0.3-0.5 pp that the third 16 px swap cost in E029/E040. If the 3-seed mean is >=0.755, or >=0.753 with a confirming rerun averaging >=0.7535, it is the new tip. Below 0.752 means the head-Muon margin is not enough to buy this swap, so try the fractional trim instead.

ideas.description: On the E044 tip, cut half of the 24 px phase using a step-indexed switch: 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 px, 7.5 total epochs. Rescale the LR warmup/decay, EMA, lookahead and renorm schedules to the new total step count, the same way the recipe already does for epoch changes. Change nothing else, and use only shapes that are already warmed up. This tests whether a fractional removal of a cheap mid-resolution epoch, which also removes Muon steps, trades better than swapping 24 px for 16 px.
ideas.expected: Time about 4.96-5.01 s (-4.5 to -5.5%): half a 24 px epoch (~0.25 s) plus ~0.02 s of Muon/per-step cost. Accuracy 0.7540-0.7560, i.e. -0.15 to -0.35 pp vs 0.7574 (Muon slope ~0.54 pp/epoch, a 24 px epoch worth ~half a 32 px one). If the loss is <=0.25 pp, the exchange rate is <=0.05 pp per 1% and fractional trimming becomes the fine-tuning knob for the remaining margin. A loss of >=0.4 pp means the 24 px bridge is binding at its current length.

ideas.description: On the E044 tip, change only the Muon learning rate of the classifier head group (the [100, 576] weight added in E044) from 0.24x to 0.5x of the filter Muon LR, i.e. 0.12 peak on the same schedule shape. A loss of >=0.4 pp means capacity stays expensive under Muon on CIFAR-100, which closes width cuts.

I've added 8 new ideas and dropped I053; I040 is still marked running. E044 (classifier head moved to Muon) gave 0.7574 at 5.237 s, about 0.44 pp above the 0.753 bar, so the queue now focuses on spending that margin.

**Spending the margin (two cuts):**
- **Third 16 px epoch, priority 5.** Port the 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 schedule onto E044. This was a near-miss in E029/E040. Expected about 5.00 s (around -4.5%) at 0.7525-0.755, so it is roughly a coin flip on feasibility.
- **Fractional trim, priority 4 (H2.10).** Remove half of the 24 px phase with a step-indexed switch, giving 7.5 epochs. Expected similar time to the swap above, with a possibly smaller loss (0.754-0.756), because it also removes Muon steps.

**Making sure the margin is real:**
- **Margin check, priority 3 (H4.2.3, rebased onto E044).** An identical rerun of E044 plus a side run on seeds 3-10. E044's +0.32 pp gain comes from a single run, and the noise on a difference between two runs is about 0.2 pp.

**Zero-cost accuracy knobs:**
- **Head Muon learning rate at 0.5x, priority 3 (H7).** The head's update size was copied from the conv filters without tuning, and E044 just showed the head is a real accuracy lever.
- **Halved warmup, priority 2 (H6.4.1, rebased onto E044).**

**Cuts that should carry over to the official 300 W PCIe GPU:**
- **Group 2 width 352, priority 3 (H2.13.1).** It reduces compute, so it should hold up on the slower judging GPU. With Muon's flatter epoch slope it may now trade at 0.06 pp or less per 1% of time.
- **Faster prepare, priority 2 (H2.4).** Prepare's ~60 ms is ~1% of the run and is no longer hidden behind power-capped training.

**Measurement:**
- **Per-phase profiling, priority 2 (H2.4.2).** It splits each phase into augmentation, forward/backward, optimizer and idle gaps. The result decides whether CUDA graphs (H2.12.1) or pre-downsampling the data for the low-res phases are worth running.

**Dropped:** I053. Its base (E035 at bs 1024) is out of date, its best case saves under 1.6%, and the profiling run measures the same small-map cost floor anyway.

**Deliberately left out:**
- **Muon LR floor (H6.5.1):** a low prior, since lowering the LR floor didn't help under SGD (E015).
- **Muon tuning:** already closed (momentum, LR, Newton-Schulz count and label smoothing all gave nothing usable).
- **Batch-size changes:** exhausted (E043).
